_README: A41a — a curated lexicon of endodontic TERMS OF ART, for RB's review.
NOT IN USE. Nothing reads this file yet. A41a's instruction was that RB
reviews it before it is used; A41b wires it in as AVAILABLE vocabulary,
never as a mandatory expansion, and measures recovery with and without.
WHY THIS EXISTS. A33g's vocabulary half failed, and why it failed is the
transferable part. The enrichment that recovered 2 of 4 target papers
contained 'orifice barrier' — not a synonym for an access restoration but
a DIFFERENT NAMED TECHNIQUE, and the phrase in both papers' titles. Asked
to expand a scenario group the generator returns synonyms of the words it
was given; five generations across two framings never produced it. A
general-purpose generator cannot invent a term of art it has no reason to
reach for.
WHY IT IS HAND-CURATED AND NOT MINED. Both were tried. Mining the
library's own titles for phrases the generator never writes returns 276
candidates and MISSES THE TWO TERMS THIS FILE EXISTS FOR: 'orifice
barrier' appears in 1 library title and 'bony lid' in 0. The library was
assembled by the retrieval that has the blind spot, so it cannot testify
about it — you cannot mine a blind spot out of a corpus collected through
it. Mining the outside corpus instead (competitor answers, the comparison
set, the titles of papers the failed fixtures name) does surface the right
terms — intraorifice barrier, direct coronal restoration, computerized
intraosseous — but buried in document furniture ('captured verbatim',
'--- banner'), because those files are commentary, not clinical prose.
So every entry below is justified by a named fixture and a PMID that was
actually missed. That is a short list on purpose. RB extends it; nothing
is added here on a hunch.
SHAPE. `head` is the canonical name. `variants` are the spellings PubMed
records actually use, and are what would be OR-ed into a group. `why`
names the fixture. `evidence` names papers the vocabulary reaches that
retrieval missed without it.

terms.head: orifice barrier
terms.concept: a material seal placed over the root filling at the canal orifice, beneath the coronal restoration
terms.why: A33 — the GIC-through-a-ceramic-crown fixture. Adding these two variants took recovery from 0/4 to 2/4; without them the query returns generic GIC-in-endodontics.

terms.head: bony lid
terms.concept: raising and replacing a cortical bone plate to reach an apex through thick mandibular cortex
terms.why: A23 — the apicoectomy fixture calls these papers 'absent entirely'. The technique exists specifically for the anatomy the question is about.

terms.head: targeted endodontic microsurgery
terms.concept: apical surgery located by a printed guide or navigation rather than by freehand estimation
terms.why: A23 names 'targeted EMS with 3D-printed guides' among the content the curriculum should have covered and did not.

terms.head: direct coronal restoration
terms.concept: restoring the crown of an endodontically treated tooth directly, without an indirect restoration
terms.why: A33c — the 2026 Cochrane review's own title. NARROWED ON CHECKING: the first draft listed 'direct restoration', 'coronal restoration' and 'post-endodontic restoration' as variants and claimed the generator had never written them. It has written all three. Only the full four-word phrase is novel, and vocabulary is not this paper's barrier anyway — ENDO_DOMAIN_FILTER excludes it from every live query, so it is reachable only from the library. Kept at low value, not deleted, because the phrase is still the field's name for the thing.

terms.head: computerized intraosseous anaesthesia
terms.concept: a powered intraosseous delivery system, distinct from conventional infiltration or block
terms.why: A25's first instance — the anaesthesia second-opinion fixture names the device; no generated query has ever contained it. Variant 'intraosseous injection' REMOVED 2026-09-05: it names the general technique, not the device, and the generator has written it (4 times in the audit log) while never writing the device term (0). The entry's claim is about the DEVICE and is still true; the variant list was over-broad and made a true claim look false.

terms.head: Kim-Kratchman classification
terms.concept: the A/B/C case-difficulty classification for apical microsurgery
terms.why: A23 lists it among the content the apicoectomy curriculum omitted.

terms.head: endodontic microsurgery
terms.concept: apical surgery under the operating microscope with ultrasonic root-end preparation — the modern name for the procedure a clinician still calls an apicoectomy
terms.why: A39a. The generated apicoectomy MODULE query reaches 1 of A23's 5 named papers. The seven-angle Literature union reaches 4 — and every one of the three extra papers arrives on ONE angle, the one containing this vocabulary. Terms 2-6 added 297 papers and zero targets. Adding this cluster (with `bony lid`) to the SINGLE query reaches the same 4 of 5, at 8 esearch calls instead of 56 and a pool of 162 instead of 435.
terms.note: MARKED TRUE, and that is the point. This is not a term the generator cannot produce — it produced it on 1 of 7 angles. It is a term it does not produce RELIABLY, and the curriculum path generates exactly one query, so it gets the vocabulary only by luck. A14 says term generation varies run to run; the lexicon is what makes it deterministic. A blind spot and an unreliable reach need the same fix and are distinguished here rather than conflated.

rejected.head: medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw
rejected.why_rejected: A23 names MRONJ/antiresorptive among the content the apicoectomy curriculum omitted, so it looked like a lexicon entry. Checked against pubmed_audit.jsonl, the generator has already written EVERY ONE of these five variants. It is not a vocabulary blind spot, and whatever went wrong on that curriculum went wrong somewhere else. Kept here rather than deleted so the same entry is not proposed again.
